situation:
You are the operations manager at FERNBROOK SANDWICH COMPANY, a two-year-old franchise with eleven shops. The founder (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should cover its next six months of payroll, now that most of its first round of funding has been spent.

SWIFTPLATE DELIVERY has offered a large payment up front for a six-month exclusive listing. The offer routes every order through the platform's tablet, puts a timer over each sandwich, and keeps the customer list, so the shop crews would no longer know which regular customers are ordering, or why the ones who stopped stopped.

One course is to accept the platform's payment up front. It covers payroll without touching anyone's pay, but it replaces the counter conversation the brand was built on with a timer screen, and the company loses the customer information its managers use to bring regular customers back.

The other course is to turn down the platform payment and cover the six months by trimming the shop crews' quarterly bonus. That keeps the counter conversation and the customer list, but takes money out of the pay of the crews whose work carries the company's name. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
